title: Level 3 (Advanced) - C-1
notes:
West leads the ♠8 against 3NT. West's lead is won by South with the ♠J. There are 7 top tricks (the spade trick just won, 3 hearts, 2 diamonds, and the ♣A). South should try to develop 2 extra tricks in diamonds.

For this to be possible, diamonds must be 3-3. A diamond trick will have to be lost and South should gear his play towards losing that trick to West. Should East gain the lead in diamonds, the defense may be in a position to take 4 spade tricks.

South should cross to the dummy in hearts and lead a diamond towards his hand. If East follows with the ♦7, the lowest outstanding diamond, South ducks and West must win the trick. The contract is safe as West cannot attack spades profitably from his side of the table.

If East plays a diamond other than the ♦7, South wins the trick and crosses again in hearts. Dummy's other diamond is played, South ducking as before if East plays the ♦7. If East does not play the ♦7, South wins and plays a third round. As long as East started with the ♦7 (and the suit is 3-3), West will have to win this trick) and the contract will be safe.
